calc-01-c2.text: Gilbert Strang, Edwin Herman et al (2016). Calculus Volume 1, Section 2.2 The Limit of a Function. OpenStax (Rice University).
calc-01-c2.quote: if the limit from the left and the limit from the right take on different values, the limit of the function does not exist.
calc-01-c2.claim: If the two sides don't agree, there's no limit.

calc-01-c3.text: Gilbert Strang, Edwin Herman et al (2016). Calculus Volume 1, Section 2.4 Continuity. OpenStax (Rice University).
calc-01-c3.quote: A function f(x) is continuous at a point a if and only if the following three conditions are satisfied:
calc-01-c3.claim: f(x) is continuous at x = a when three things are true: 1. f(a) exists (the function is defined there) 2. The limit as x approaches a exists
